title: The President, at the Parade: Mexico Does Not Bow Down, Does Not Kneel, and Is Not for Sale
author: SinEmbargo
content:
_This article originally appeared in the[September 16, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4871353/la-presidenta-en-el-desfile-
mexico-no-se-doblega-no-se-arrodilla-y-no-se-vende/), a Mexican independent
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, September 16 (SinEmbargo).—** President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo
affirmed this Wednesday that “Mexico does not bow down, does not kneel, and is
not for sale.” The remarks came amid an atmosphere of tensions with the United
States (US) and on the day commemorating the start of Mexican Independence.

“September 16, Independence Day, is the living memory of Mexico. It always
means holding our heads high and shouting to the four winds that **Mexico will
never be anyone’s colony or protectorate**. Long live Independence! Long live
sovereignty! May Mexico live forever! Long live Mexico! Long live Mexico!” she
said before the start of the 2026 Military Parade.

> Mexico does not bow down, does not kneel, and Mexico is never for sale.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

From the country’s capital Zócalo, Sheinbaum Pardo stressed that “**Mexico was
born from the rebellion of a people who refused to accept injustice as their
destiny** ,” and that “independence was born of brave women and men who had
the courage to defy power.”

In her message, she recalled that thanks to this feat, Miguel Hidalgo y
Costilla is known as “the Father of the Nation.” “Even today some have sought
to diminish his heroism and his vision. Deep down, what they do not forgive
him for is that he summoned independence through a true popular rebellion,”
she noted.

At another point, she spoke of the importance of José María Morelos y Pavón in
the independence process, since he “understood a fundamental truth: weapons
can win battles, but only ideas can found nations.”

“On one side, one camp, the conservative one, centralist and monarchist in
nature, which in its desperation applauded the foreign boot and brought in
Maximilian of Habsburg. The other, the one of liberal, republican, and social-
justice ideas, which chose to give its life rather than surrender,” she added.

“Because even though some might wish otherwise, Mexico cannot be understood
without its noble, brave, and hardworking people. Nor can it be understood
without its constant struggle for sovereignty and independence,” she
maintained.

Finally, the President of Mexico added that “**freedom is conquered,
sovereignty is defended, and a just and dignified homeland is built every
day**.”
